site.name: Olea & Sale
site.tagline: A wood-fire kitchen with a Mediterranean accent. Lisbon, since 2019.

pages.title: Olea & Sale — Wood-fire kitchen in Lisbon
pages.description: A tight menu of wood-fire dishes built around the day's market. Open Tuesday through Saturday for dinner; Sundays for long lunches.

pages.title: Menu — Olea & Sale
pages.description: Tonight's menu, written this afternoon. We change roughly half the dishes each week, following what's at the market.

pages.title: About — Olea & Sale
pages.description: Twelve seats, two cooks, one fire. Why we opened, who we cook for, and where the food comes from.

pages.title: Contact & Reservations — Olea & Sale
pages.description: Reservations open four weeks in advance. Walk-ins welcome at the bar.

hero-media.headline: A wood-fire kitchen with a Mediterranean accent
hero-media.subheadline: Twelve seats, two cooks, one fire. We cook what's at the market that morning, on a wood grill, for the people who walked through the door that evening.
hero-media.mediaAlt: A whole grilled sea bream on a ceramic plate with charred lemon and salsa verde, on a marble counter at Olea & Sale.

features-grid.headline: Three things that don't change
features-grid.subheadline: The menu changes weekly. These don't.

features.title: Wood fire, every dish
features.description: Holm-oak coals, no gas burner in the building. Every plate touches the grill or the wood oven at some point in its life.

features.title: Market in the morning, plate at night
features.description: We buy at Ribeira Market most days. What's there sets the menu. If the dourada isn't right, the dourada isn't on the card.

features.title: Twelve seats, two cooks
features.description: You'll see us cook. We'll see you eat. It's harder to phone in a dish when you're three meters from the person eating it.

features.title: Wine from neighbours
features.description: Almost the entire list is Portuguese, mostly from small producers we visit. Nothing on the list costs more than 65€.

features.title: No corkage games
features.description: Bring a bottle if you must — 12€ corkage, no eye-rolling. We'd rather you drink something you love.

features.title: Long Sundays
features.description: Sunday lunch starts at 1pm and stretches as long as you want it to. Last sitting at 3:30, but no one's counting.

testimonials-grid.headline: What our guests say
testimonials-grid.subheadline: We keep a paper guestbook by the door. A few entries we asked permission to share.

items.quote: The grilled octopus was the single best plate I had in three weeks of eating across Portugal. We came back for the carrots the next night, which sounds insane but is true.
items.author: Maya Patel

items.quote: Twelve seats, no English menu when we visited, two cooks who waved at our toddler. It's the restaurant I tell every friend about. I've sent six couples here in 2025.
items.author: Diego Romero

items.quote: The wine list is one of the best in the city — short, all neighbours, all reasonable. Whoever buys for them is doing the city a service.
items.author: Soren Mikkelsen

cta-strip.headline: Come find a seat
cta-strip.subheadline: Reservations open four weeks ahead. Walk-ins welcome at the bar (six seats, first come).

features-bento.headline: What's on the fire this week
features-bento.subheadline: Roughly half the menu changes each week. Here's what we're cooking right now. Allergens noted on the printed card.

features.title: Whole grilled sea bream
features.description: Today's catch from Sesimbra, grilled over holm-oak coals with charred lemon, salsa verde, and the morning's bread. For two. 38€.

features.title: Wood-fire octopus
features.description: Slow-cooked, then finished over the grill. Smoked paprika oil, lima beans. 22€.

features.title: Charred carrots, dukkah
features.description: From a farmer in Mafra. Tahini, honey, sumac. 9€.

features.title: Côte de bœuf, for two
features.description: Eight-week dry-aged Alentejana, 800g over the coals with rosemary salt. Bone-marrow on the side. 78€ for two, 30-min cook time. Order at the start of your meal.

hero-text.headline: Twelve seats. Two cooks. One fire.
hero-text.subheadline: We opened Olea & Sale in 2019 because we missed the kind of restaurants where the cooks knew the guests by face and the food was honest about where it came from. So we built one.

how-it-works.headline: A short supply chain, by design
how-it-works.subheadline: We can name the person who grew or caught almost everything on your plate. Here's roughly how that works.

steps.title: 6:30am · Ribeira Market
steps.description: One of us is at the market every morning. We buy fish from the same three boats, vegetables from four farms, bread from a baker in Marvila.

steps.title: 10am · Menu set
steps.description: Back at the kitchen by 9. By 10 the menu is written for that night. Printed by 4pm. What you read at your table is roughly five hours old.

steps.title: 7pm · The fire is hot
steps.description: Holm-oak coals lit at 5pm; service starts at 7. From there it's two cooks, twelve seats, and three hours of focused work.

faq.headline: Questions guests ask
faq.subheadline: Email ola@oleasale.pt if yours isn't here — Ola reads everything personally.

items.question: How far in advance should I book?
items.answer: Reservations open four weeks ahead, online, at 10am Lisbon time. Friday and Saturday usually go in the first few hours. Tuesday and Wednesday are easier.

items.question: Do you take walk-ins?
items.answer: Yes, at the bar — six seats, first come, first served. We hold those exclusively for walk-ins. Come early, especially on weekends.

items.question: I have an allergy or dietary need. Can you accommodate?
items.answer: Almost always — tell us when you book and we'll plan ahead. We're not a strict vegetarian kitchen but we always have 3–4 vegetable-led dishes a night.

items.question: Is there a children's menu?
items.answer: No children's menu, but children are welcome and we'll happily portion any dish for a small person. The whole fish for two is a hit with curious 8-year-olds.

items.question: Can I bring my own wine?
items.answer: Yes — 12€ corkage, no eye-rolling, no minimum bottle value. We'd rather you drank something you loved than ordered to feel polite.

items.question: Do you do private events?
items.answer: Yes, the full room can be booked for parties of 12. Email ola@oleasale.pt with a date and we'll send a sample menu and pricing.
